{{short description|Russian-American mathematician}}
'''Gregory Beylkin''' (born 16 March 1953) is a Russian–American mathematician.<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=Gregory Beylkin {{!}} Professor|website=CU Experts {{!}} University of Colorado Boulder|url=https://experts.colorado.edu/display/fisid_100437}}</ref>

==Education and career==
He studied from 1970 to 1975 at the [[University of Leningrad]], with Diploma in Mathematics in November 1975. From 1976 to 1979 he was a research scientist at the Research Institute of Ore Geophysics, Leningrad. From 1980 to 1982 he was a graduate student at [[New York University]],<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Gregory Belkin, CV|website=CU Experts {{!}} University of Colorado Boulder|url=https://experts.colorado.edu/vitas/100437.pdf}}</ref> where he received his PhD under the supervision of [[Peter Lax]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=33690|title=Gregory Beylkin}}</ref> From 1982 to 1983 Beylkin was an associate research scientist at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]]. From 1983 to 1991 he was a member of the professional staff of [[Schlumberger#History|Schlumberger-Doll Research]] in [[Ridgefield, Connecticut]]. Since 1991 he has been a professor in the Department of Applied Mathematics at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]]. He was a visiting professor at [[Yale University]], the [[University of Minnesota]], and the [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]] and participated in 2012 and 2015 in the summer seminar on "Applied Harmonic Analysis and Sparse Approximation" at Oberwolfach. He is the author or co-author of over 100 articles in refereed journal and has served on several editorial boards.<ref name=CV/>

{{blockquote|Gregory Beylkin's research is focused on analysis and development of fast algorithms for solving integral and differential equations. Applications include [[quantum chemistry]], [[gravity field]] evaluation and estimation, [[wave propagation]] and [[inverse problems]]. A number of algorithms developed by Gregory Beylkin and his group have been implemented and are used in practical applications.<ref name=homepage/>}}

==Awards and honors==
* 1998 — Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]]<ref>{{cite book|author=Beylkin, Gregory|chapter=On multiresolution methods in numerical analysis|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=481–490|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011604000}}</ref>
* 2012 — Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]
* 2016 — Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]
